q: Which file defines a bundle's name, included resource files, variables and targets?
e: databricks.yml at the project root is the bundle configuration. Resources are usually split into files under resources/ and pulled in with include.

q: After `databricks bundle deploy -t dev`, the scheduled job doesn't start on its schedule. Why?
o: Development mode pauses schedules and triggers
Schedules only work with job clusters
The job must be run with bundle run first
e: mode: development prefixes resource names with [dev user] and pauses schedules, so dev copies don't run on their own.

q: A CI pipeline must pass a database password to the bundle at deploy time without storing it in Git. What do you use?
o: Write it into databricks.yml under the prod target
Set it as the BUNDLE_VAR_<name> environment variable from the CI secret store
Put it in the variable's default value
e: BUNDLE_VAR_<name> environment variables override bundle variables, and their values can come from the CI system's secret store.

q: Production jobs must not run with the identity of the engineer who deployed them. Which bundle setting handles this?
o: `run_as` with a service principal on the prod target
e: run_as sets the identity that jobs and pipelines run with. Production mode validates it, and a service principal is the recommended choice.

q: In which order should a CI/CD pipeline typically run the bundle commands for a staging deployment?
e: validate catches configuration errors, deploy creates or updates the resources, and run executes the job, e.g. integration tests, against the deployed version.
